title: An envelope taped under Gus's bench in Astoria Park: C$800 in twenties and a note, 'for Marisol's rent.'

options.label: Give it to Gus
options.riskWhy: Gus knows everyone in the park

outcomes.text: Gus counts it twice and nods once. 'Marisol cleans the chapel. This is her whole month.' He shakes your hand like it's a contract.

later.text: Remember the envelope under Gus's bench? Marisol found you in the park with a tray of pastelitos and C$150 she would not take back.
later.headline: Developing: {name} handed back C$800 in rent money found under a park bench in Astoria. Sources say Gus now calls them 'the kid.' 👀

options.label: Pocket the envelope
options.riskWhy: Gus never really sleeps on that bench

outcomes.text: You peel the envelope off like a sticker. C$800. Gus is asleep, or doing a very good impression.
You walk off C$800 richer. Gus opens one eye, then closes it. Somehow that's worse.

later.text: Remember the envelope under Gus's bench? Gus told the park, the park told Sgt. Bev. You paid it back from the holding bench.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} spent the afternoon on the 114½ Precinct's bench over C$800 lifted from a park bench. Sgt. Bev: 'Bench to bench. Poetic.'

options.label: Take half, tape back half
options.riskWhy: Half a theft is still a theft

outcomes.text: You take C$400 and tape the rest back, neatly. A compromise with yourself that nobody else asked for.

later.text: Remember the half-empty envelope? Marisol pinned the note up at the chapel: 'Whoever took half, God saw. So did Gus.' The park side-eyes you.

title: A phone left at Grind & Gossip lights up: 'Reward if found: C$100.' A guy by the door offers C$450 for it.

options.label: Give it to Jojo
options.get: C$100 and a friend for life

outcomes.text: The owner, a frantic grad student, runs in and cries. She sends C$100. Jojo writes your name on the regulars' wall in foam-heart pen.

options.label: Sell it to the guy
options.riskWhy: The café has a camera. And Jojo.

outcomes.text: C$450, folded twice, no questions. The phone's gone before your coffee cools.
C$450, folded twice. Jojo is very still behind the machine.

later.text: Remember the phone at Grind & Gossip? Jojo checked the tape. You're banned for a week, and the owner's post has 3,000 shares.
later.headline: BREAKING: Grind & Gossip bans {name} for a week after a lost phone 'walked off.' Jojo, on the record: 'I make foam hearts. I also check the tape.'

outcomes.text: You text the owner: 'C$250 and it's yours.' She pays. She also posts your text, with a lot of crying emojis.
She pays C$250 and says thank you. You feel strange about it, which is correct.

title: Rev. Mercy hands you the roof fund, C$2,400 in a zip bag, to drop at the bank. 'I trust you, child.'

outcomes.text: The teller counts C$2,400 out loud. Rev. Mercy gets the text and sends back nine praying-hands emojis.

later.text: Remember the roof fund? The new roof is on, and your name ended up on the donor plaque by mistake. Rev. Mercy says leave it.

outcomes.text: C$2,500 goes in. Rev. Mercy reads your name out on Sunday. The choir does a little run on it.

options.label: Skim C$600, blame the bake sale

outcomes.text: C$1,800 goes in. 'They must have miscounted at the bake sale,' you say. Rev. Mercy just looks at you for a long time.

later.text: Remember the roof fund? The bake-sale ladies had spreadsheets. Rev. Mercy forgave you in the sermon, by name, and asked you to stay away a week.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} forgiven, by name, in Sunday's sermon at Harmony Chapel over C$600 missing from the roof fund. The choir gasped in harmony.

title: Captain Rosa's calendar money, C$1,500, needs counting. She's up a ladder. Hydrant is eating the receipts.

outcomes.text: C$1,500 exactly, rubber-banded by hundreds. Rosa yells 'Wepa!' from the ladder.

later.text: Remember counting the calendar money? Captain Rosa put you in the calendar. February. Holding Hydrant, who is holding a helmet.

options.label: Skim C$400, blame the dog
options.riskWhy: Rosa knows what Hydrant can eat

outcomes.text: C$1,100 goes in the box. 'Hydrant got some,' you say. Hydrant looks offended.
C$1,100 in the box. Hydrant wags. Rosa climbs down slowly.

later.text: Remember the calendar money? Hydrant didn't eat the receipts, he buried them. Rosa dug them up and called Sgt. Bev, who loves a dog story.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} blamed a dalmatian for C$400 missing from Engine 7's calendar fund. The dalmatian has been cleared. Sgt. Bev: 'Good boy.'

outcomes.text: C$1,450 in the box and a C$50 bagel run for you. Nobody notices. You notice.

title: Sgt. Bev waves at her lost-and-found bin: 'Point at whatever's yours, hon.' There's a C$1,500 watch.

outcomes.text: Bev looks up from her mug for the first time all day. 'Huh.' She writes something down. That's the service.

later.text: Remember the lost-and-found at the 114½? Sgt. Bev told Lola you were the only honest one at her desk all week. Lola ran it.
later.headline: Developing: Sgt. Bev Kowalski of the 114½ calls {name} 'the only honest person at my desk this week.' She adds: 'It was a slow week.'

outcomes.text: Bev slides it over without looking. 'Sign here, here and here. Triplicate.' A shop in Flushing gives you C$1,500.
Bev slides it over. You sign in triplicate and sell it in Flushing for C$1,500.

later.text: Remember the watch from the 114½? Its real owner came in with a photo. Bev called you back, sighed for nine minutes and booked you.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} booked for claiming a stranger's watch from the 114½ Precinct's own lost-and-found. Sgt. Bev: 'At my desk. With my pen.'

outcomes.text: 'That one.' Bev doesn't even look. It's cashmere-ish. You feel sort of cashmere-ish about it.

title: A delivery van on Steinway, back door open: forty boxes of Dunk Daniels 9s. A crew: 'Lookout pays C$600.'

options.label: Keep walking
options.riskWhy: Not your van, not your problem

outcomes.text: You keep walking. Behind you, someone yells 'yo, the driver!' and forty boxes go back in a van. Probably.

options.label: Text Sgt. Bev the plate
options.riskWhy: The crew might see you texting

outcomes.text: Bev rolls up eating a pierogi. The crew scatters. The courier company sends you C$300 and a very formal thank-you.
Bev arrives in four minutes, which she calls 'a personal best.' The crew saw you texting.

later.text: Remember the van on Steinway? The crew left one left-foot sneaker on your doorstep. Message received. Your block feels colder.

options.label: Be the lookout
options.cost: Your name on a crew's list

outcomes.text: You stare at a pigeon for six minutes. C$600 lands in your hand. You are, technically, in a crew now.

later.text: Remember the van on Steinway? The crew's back. They have a bigger van in mind, and you in the driver's seat.

outcomes.text: Sgt. Bev's cruiser turns the corner. Everyone runs. You run worst. 'You were the lookout? You were looking at a pigeon.'

options.label: Grab a box yourself
options.cost: Being the one holding the box

outcomes.text: A reseller on Ditmars takes the box by sundown: C$1,400, cash.
The driver comes back with his coffee. You're holding the box. He just points. Sgt. Bev does the rest.

later.text: Remember the sneaker van? Lola got the precinct log. Your booking photo is her most-liked post this week.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} caught holding a box of Dunk Daniels 9s off a Steinway delivery van. Sgt. Bev: 'Size 11. I checked.'

title: Outside Meteor Park, a crew unloads a merch truck that isn't theirs. 'Carry two, keep one: C$500.'

options.label: Head for your seat
options.riskWhy: You saw nothing, you know nothing

outcomes.text: You find Section 7. Hector says you look like someone who just made a good decision.

options.label: Tell Hector the usher
options.riskWhy: The crew knows your face now

outcomes.text: Hector radios it in. Security saves the truck. The Meteors send two seats behind the dugout to 'our hero in 7.'
Hector radios it in. The crew is long gone, and one of them waves at you from the 7 train. Cute.

options.label: Carry two, keep one
options.riskWhy: Stadiums have cameras on every gate

outcomes.text: Two boxes carried, one kept. A jersey reseller in Flushing pays C$500 and doesn't ask which player.

later.text: Remember the jerseys at Meteor Park? The crew liked your work. They have a bigger van in mind, and you in the driver's seat.

outcomes.text: The gate camera zooms in like it's a replay. Stadium security bans you for the week and hands you to Sgt. Bev, who is a Meteors fan.

title: The crew is back: 'Next van's electronics. You drive. C$2,500.' They already know where you live.

outcomes.text: You hand over C$800 'for the inconvenience.' They shrug and delete your number. You're out, and broke-ish.

options.label: Drive the van
options.riskWhy: Sgt. Bev knows this crew by name

outcomes.text: You drive like a grandmother on a Sunday. C$2,500. Nobody notices a thing.
Bev pulls the van over for a broken taillight. She opens the back. She sighs so hard her radio crackles.

later.text: Remember the van? Lola has the photos. So does everyone you've ever met.
later.headline: BREAKING: {name} pulled over on 31st Street in a van of 'definitely ours' electronics. Sgt. Bev: 'Taillight's out too. Rough day.'

options.label: Tell Sgt. Bev everything
options.get: A clean slate, maybe a reward

outcomes.text: Bev listens, eats a pierogi and writes it all down. 'Go home, hon.' The crew gets picked up Tuesday. The courier company sends C$500.

later.text: Remember telling Sgt. Bev about the crew? She told Lola. Lola made you sound like a movie.

outcomes.text: Bev thanks you, then books you for the lookout job. 'Rules, hon. One hour. I'll get you a coffee.'

title: Mr. Penwright's book sale: a signed first edition priced C$2 by mistake. A collector in Flushing pays C$1,800.

outcomes.text: Penwright removes his glasses, polishes them and puts them back on. 'Good heavens.' He shakes your hand for an uncomfortably long time.

later.text: Remember the first edition? The library auctioned it for a new reading corner. The little plaque says 'Thanks to an honest reader.' It's you.
later.headline: Developing: a signed first edition priced C$2 at the Ditmars Free Library went to auction thanks to {name}. Mr. Penwright: 'Good heavens.'

options.label: Buy it, sell it in Flushing

outcomes.text: Two dollars at the desk. C$1,800 in Flushing. The collector calls you 'a person of taste.'
C$2 in, C$1,800 out. The collector posts it, with the library's stamp in the corner of the photo.

later.text: Remember the C$2 first edition? Penwright saw his own stamp online. You're buying it back at C$2,000 and staying out of the library for a week.

options.label: Buy it for your shelf
options.riskWhy: It's on your shelf, not on sale

outcomes.text: C$2. It looks incredible on your shelf. You will never read it.
